devdoc.title: FairTickets (commit-reveal version), for Quai Orchard, where Chainlink VRF isn't available.

acceptOffer(uint256).notice: A waitlisted fan accepts an offered seat by paying face value.

assistedRegister(address,bytes32).notice: Assisted desk: staff checked a passport / other ID in person. Only a hash of the document is stored. Capped and publicly counted, so it can't become a back door, and the same document can't register twice.

checkTicket(uint256).notice: Everything the public ticket checker needs in one call.

claimTicket(uint256).notice: A lottery winner pays face value to receive the ticket for their seat.

commitInventory(bytes32,uint32,uint32,ui.notice: Lock the seat inventory before the sale. Can only be done once.

commitSeed(bytes32).notice: Organiser commits keccak256(abi.encode(secret)) before registration opens.

expireOffer(uint256).notice: Move an expired offer on to the next waitlisted fan. Anyone can call.

fallbackDraw().notice: If the organiser never reveals, anyone can run the draw from recent block hashes.

getEntrantsPage(uint256,uint256).notice: A page of the entrant list (shuffled order once drawn), for large events.

getLiveTickets().notice: All live tickets — fine for small events; large events use getLiveTicketsPage.

getLiveTicketsPage(uint256,uint256).notice: Live tickets with ids in [fromId, fromId + count): gate scanners sync in pages.

passScope().notice: Event scope for Fan Pass proofs: unique per event, below the SNARK field.

positionOf(address).notice: Final position of `fan` in the shuffled list (0 = first winner), or type(uint256).max if they didn't register or their slot hasn't been drawn yet. O(1) at any event size.

register(uint256,uint256,uint256[4],uint.notice: Register for the lottery with an Anon Aadhaar proof. The proof's signal must be the caller's address, so a copied proof is useless to anyone else.

registerWithPass(address,(uint256,uint25.notice: Register `fan` with a Fan Pass proof (seconds on a phone). The proof's message must be the fan's wallet, so anyone (e.g. a gas relayer) may submit it without being able to redirect the entry.

releaseUnclaimed(uint256).notice: After the claim window, unclaimed winning seats go to the waitlist. Anyone can call.

requestDraw().notice: After registration closes, anyone can freeze the list and fix the future draw block.

revealSeats(uint256[],string[],bytes32[].notice: Prove public seats belong to the committed inventory. Anyone can call this. Leaves follow OpenZeppelin's StandardMerkleTree: keccak256(keccak256(abi.encode(index, label, category, salt))).

revealSeed(bytes32).notice: Organiser reveals the committed secret once the draw block has been mined.

runShuffle(uint256).notice: Run `steps` steps of the Fisher–Yates shuffle. Anyone can call; batched for large events.

sellBack(uint256).notice: Return your ticket. You are refunded face value when the next fan takes the seat.

setAssistedCap(uint32).notice: Organiser sets the public quota for the assisted desk (fans without Aadhaar: foreign visitors, minors with a guardian). Fixed before registration opens.

setFanPass(address,bool).notice: Organiser links the Fan Pass registry before registration opens. With `passOnly`, real fans can ONLY enter with a Fan Pass (direct Aadhaar entry is closed), so one person can't use both routes for two entries. All-zero proofs still reach the verifier: only the labelled demo router accepts those, for its listed synthetic accounts.

userdoc.notice: Randomness = keccak256(organiser secret, hash of a block mined AFTER registration closed).  1. Before registration opens, the organiser commits keccak256(secret) on-chain.  2. After registration closes, requestDraw() freezes the entrant list and picks a FUTURE block.  3. The organiser reveals the secret; the seed mixes it with that block's hash. The organiser can't change the secret (it was committed before anyone registered), and when committing they couldn't know the future block hash. If the organiser refuses to reveal, anyone can trigger a fallback draw after REVEAL_WINDOW blocks, so withholding can't stall the sale. Honest limitation: the organiser could withhold a reveal they dislike, forcing the fallback seed; they still can't choose the result.
